brief: Minors and observations left by JS-159 and JS-161 (brief-triage-0523.md): a segment re-read on every poll; an unmeasurable segment held with no trace; the exit-first order covered only by natural runs (failed 2 of 32 on main, 20 of 20 after the fix); failures not countable across a restart, so JS-159 criterion 6 could not be taken; a run returned clean with QA items unfinished; nine capacity and admission notes on JS-161; JS-161's recorded jellyfin-web measurements not done.
tradeoff: Given up: the dogfood count of jobs that failed after storing a segment before the fix (JS-159 criterion 6), so whether a cut-short segment was stored there is not known, and any leaves with transcodeRetention; a forced check of the exit-first order; two of three second-viewer runs of each kind and the developer-machine shared-play runs of JS-161. No viewer or operator loses a capability.
entry: No new task and no priority moved. JS-175 criterion 7 counts the two cut-read cases apart in its 10 queue runs, one failure returning JS-159 as a brief; no hook in the worker. JS-176 gains criterion 5: /metrics shows as capacity for new plays only what admission counts while a worker is unmeasured. JS-164 criterion 2: a held-film refusal carries its own reason from whichever replica refuses. JS-079 gains criterion 5: a worker of the previous release is not counted as a partner for a shared play unless it says it can help. JS-159 criterion 6 is closed as not taken; docs/running.md says jellyscale keeps no history of ended jobs and that counts across restarts come from scraping /metrics and keeping logs; no failure history is built. JS-161's shared-play measurement is taken by JS-166 criterion 3 on the dogfood, and its second-viewer measurement is one run of each kind beside the next task. docs/transcoding.md marks the i5-6500's 2.7 as computed until the dogfood's measured figure replaces it; the SMT question and the single-benchmark question are answered by that reading and JS-166 criterion 9. Backlog: BL-253 (segment re-read per poll), BL-254 (unmeasurable segment held silently), BL-255 (a clean run with QA items unfinished; build.js changes on a second occurrence), BL-256 (stale shared-placed queued job holds cores), BL-257 (timed-out measurement counted at reference speed; promoted on a dogfood measurement over 7.5 s or a timed-out line), BL-258 (a film held 60 s after its viewer leaves). JS-176 starts now; JS-174 runs beside it, never ahead. Reopens on: a cut-read failure in the counted runs; an early-input-end failure counted on the dogfood after the fix; the dogfood's measured capacities changing which rows a node holds.
serves: PRODUCT.md: 'every failure is reported with its reason, never silent'; 'Nothing breaks the viewers' evening. Upgrades, a lost machine and a database failover happen without interrupting anyone.' DOMAINS.md invariant 40. Owner, 2026-11-22: nothing outruns the product.
